snippet.title: Timber Longplay (Arcade Game)
snippet.description:
- Timber Longplay (Arcade Game) -

Timber, released by Bally Midway in 1984, is a fast-paced arcade action game built around chopping down trees under time pressure. You play as a lumberjack who must clear a series of forested areas before the timer runs out, swinging your axe in quick bursts while trees continuously pop up around the screen. Each tree takes several hits to fell, and every swing changes your character’s facing direction, giving the game a steady rhythm that rewards quick reactions.

Although the premise is simple, Timber becomes demanding due to the increasing speed and the number of hazards appearing in later stages. Falling branches, angry bears charging across the screen, and swarms of bees add constant pressure, forcing players to move carefully while still maintaining a fast chopping pace. Periodically, the gameplay shifts to a log-balancing bonus round, where staying upright on a rotating log earns extra points and grants a brief break from the main action.

Timber also includes a two-player simultaneous mode, allowing both players to chop together on the same screen. This creates a blend of cooperation and friendly competition, as each tries to clear trees efficiently while navigating around the other player. The shared space encourages either teamwork or playful interference, depending on who you’re playing with.

Visually, Timber uses bright, bold sprites typical of early-80s Midway titles. The action is easy to read even as the screen fills with newly spawning trees and hazards. Sound effects are simple but functional, giving snappy audio feedback for swings, falls, and bonuses without adding clutter.

Timber remains a straightforward example of early arcade design: quick to learn, demanding in the long run, and built around fast reflexes and score-chasing. While not as widely known as some of Bally Midway’s other titles of the era, it offers a distinct style of pressure-filled, timing-based gameplay that still holds interest today.
